Python commands for your marble run

ramp(x1, y1, x2, y2)

Adds a piece of cardboard from point (x1, y1) to point (x2, y2). All numbers are centimeters. The box goes from x = -55 (left) to x = 55 (right) and from y = 0 (floor) to y = 80 (top). 
ramp(-50, 70, 20, 60)   # slopes down to the right
Add a color name as a 5th value if you want: ramp(-50, 70, 20, 60, "red")

wall(x, y_bottom, y_top)

A straight-up-and-down piece of cardboard. Great for stopping the marble so it drops. 
wall(30, 10, 25)

Variables

drop = 8          # how much each ramp falls
top = 72
ramp(-54, top, 48, top - drop)

Loops (the smart way to build a zig-zag)

y = 72
for i in range(4):
    if i % 2 == 0:
        ramp(-54, y, 48, y - 8)    # going right
    else:
        ramp(54, y, -48, y - 8)    # going left
    y = y - 13

print()

Shows a message in the black console. Use it to check your math: print("Next ramp starts at", y)

Physics tips

  • A steeper ramp makes the marble faster. A flatter ramp is slower, but too flat and it gets stuck.
  • Longer paths = more time. The side walls of the box bounce the marble back, so zig-zags work.
  • A fast marble flies off the end of a ramp. Use a wall to catch it.
  • Hover your mouse over the box to read coordinates. Drag to spin the view, scroll to zoom.
